climbing_route.label: South Chute
climbing_route.notes: Turn south into the South Chute at the 'Cat Ears' rock landmark. A long, narrowing scree gully climbing about 1,900 ft from the lake to roughly 6,600 ft. Loose underfoot and much better done on residual early-season snow, since bare scree here is notoriously miserable and can sluff rock onto parties below.

climbing_route.label: Saddle and second scree gully to the notch
climbing_route.notes: Above the chute, cross a saddle, drop about 150 ft, and work up a second scree gully to a notch in the summit ridge.

climbing_route.label: Gaps and ledges to the traverse
climbing_route.notes: From the notch the route threads gaps and ledges, marked in places by faded white-paint dots, to the base of the Finger Traverse itself.

climbing_route.label: Finger Traverse
climbing_route.notes: An exposed, downsloping ledge above a large cliff, where climbers jam their fingers into a crack running along the top edge for balance. A rusty, decades-old set of fixed pitons sits along the ledge for parties who want to protect it, though most cross carefully unroped. Figure 5-6+ hours above the lake to the summit.
